record.title: JERA, Dell and RHAELM plan up to 400 MW of AI data-center infrastructure in Chiba
record.summary: On 2026-10-01, JERA, Dell Technologies and RHAELM announced an MoU to develop a standardized AI-infrastructure model in Japan. They named JERA’s Chiba thermal power station as the first planned site and said they would develop up to 400,000 kW of AI data-center infrastructure there using an integrated model for power generation, electricity infrastructure, cooling and AI compute. The partners expect total project investment above US$15 billion across land, power infrastructure, facility construction and AI compute, and target operation around 2028. These are plans reported by the counterparties; the announcement does not establish financing close, permits, construction, energized capacity or actual IT load.

claims.label: CLAIMED
claims.text: JERA says JERA, Dell Technologies and RHAELM signed an MoU on 2026-10-01 to develop a standardized national AI-infrastructure concept, and identifies the JERA Chiba station as the first planned project.

claims.label: CLAIMED
claims.text: The partners say they plan to develop up to 400,000 kW of AI data-center infrastructure at the Chiba station, integrating power generation, electricity infrastructure, cooling and AI compute. The source does not define the figure as IT load.

claims.label: CLAIMED
claims.text: The partners expect total investment above US$15 billion across land, power infrastructure, facility construction and AI computing capacity, and target operation around 2028.

claims.label: NOT_ESTABLISHED
claims.text: The announcement does not establish a financing close, final investment decision, permits, completed construction, delivered accelerators, energized IT capacity or utilization.

evidence_gaps.description: No project-specific financing close/FID, permit or construction record was inspected; the source describes an MoU and plans.
The announcement does not specify whether up to 400,000 kW refers to total facility infrastructure capacity, IT load or another capacity basis.
No accelerator deliveries, energized compute, utilization or realized operating date were established.

brief.importance_rationale: If executed at the announced scale, this project could materially change Japanese AI compute capacity and data-center power delivery, and demonstrate an integrated on-site model for a market facing grid-connection lead times. The score is major but below field-shifting because the evidence is an MoU and partner plan, the 400 MW figure is not defined as IT load, and financing, permits, construction and operation are unestablished.
limitations: This record is about counterparties’ announced plan, not a financed or operating project.
The up-to-400,000 kW figure is described as AI data-center infrastructure; it is not defined as IT load.
The >US$15B expected total covers land, electricity infrastructure, facility construction and AI compute across project scope; it is not a confirmed facility-only construction budget.
No project-specific FID, financing close, permit, construction, accelerator delivery, energized capacity, utilization or realized operation was inspected.

They named JERA’s Chiba thermal power station as the first planned site and said they would develop up to 400,000 kW of AI data-center infrastructure there using an integrated model for power generation, electricity infrastructure, cooling and AI compute. technical.claimed_result: The partners plan up to 400,000 kW of AI data-center infrastructure, expect more than US$15B of total project investment, and target operation around 2028.
technical.compute_or_cost: The source gives more than US$15B as expected total investment across land, power infrastructure, facility construction and AI computing capacity. No cost allocation, capex close, electricity price, accelerator count or cost per IT MW is provided.
technical.demonstrated_result: The primary source demonstrates that the counterparties announced an MoU and a planned Chiba project. It does not demonstrate construction, available compute or operating performance.
technical.implementation_status: MoU and planning announcement only in the inspected source. Financing/FID, permitting, construction, equipment delivery and operation are not established.
technical.mechanism: The parties propose integrating JERA’s existing thermal-station site and on-site electricity supply with Dell’s standardized rack-scale AI infrastructure and RHAELM’s data-center development role, alongside cooling and compute infrastructure.
technical.novelty: The announced first site couples an existing thermal-power-station setting and on-site power with standardized AI data-center infrastructure; the partners describe a possible repeatable model, not a demonstrated deployment.
technical.regime: One proposed AI-infrastructure project at JERA’s Chiba thermal power station, within an MoU covering a standardized power-to-compute model. The 400,000 kW capacity basis is unspecified.
technical.reproducibility: Not a research experiment. Verify the project through later primary financing, permits, construction, commissioning and operating-capacity disclosures.
technical.strongest_baseline: The partners compare their intended on-site model with conventional grid-connected data-center development and claim it could deliver AI compute capacity several years earlier; no independent matched baseline or schedule analysis was reviewed.

brief.title: JERA, Dell and RHAELM plan up to 400 MW of AI data-center infrastructure in Chiba
brief.why_it_matters: If carried out, a 400 MW-scale AI data-center infrastructure plan paired with on-site power at an existing Japanese thermal station could materially affect compute availability and the economics of data-center development in Japan. The proposed standardized integration of power, cooling and compute also offers a model the partners say they may extend. The scale, timing and deployment remain unverified beyond the parties’ announcement, and 400 MW is not defined as IT load.
